header.running_head: The Manner in which Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Distributed Wealth

blocks.text: they neither found a Dinaar nor a Dirham. All they found was a coarse cloth for storing money and when they shook it, all that emerged was a single Dirham. They all then prayed for Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA). There was a man in Madinah who weighed Dinaars and Dirhams even during the time of Rasulullaah ﷺ. It was he who used to do the weighing for Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) as well. When he was asked what the value of the wealth was that came to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he replied that it amounted to two hundred thousand.[^1]
The Narration of Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad and others about the Fairness in the Manner that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Distributed Wealth

Hadhrat Ismaa'eel bin Muhammad reports that whenever Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) distributed wealth amongst the people he always gave equally. Hadhrat Umar (RA) once objected saying, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! How can you give the same to the veterans of Badr as you give to other people?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "The things of this world are merely a means of existence and the best of such means are those that are moderate (and this applies equally to all people). The superiority of the veterans of Badr shall be seen in their rewards (in the Aakhirah).[^2]

Another narration states that when it was mentioned to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) that he ought to give preference to some people in the distribution of wealth, he said, "Their virtues shall be rewarded by Allaah (in the Aakhirah). With regard to their worldly existence, equality is best."[^3]

Yet another narration from Hadhrat Aslam states that when Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) became the Khalifah and distributed equally amongst the people, someone said to him, "O Khalifah of Rasulullaah ﷺ! Why do you not give preference to the Muhaajireen and the Ansaar (by giving them a larger share)?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) replied, "Should I buy their virtues from them? With regard to people's existence in this world, equality is better than showing preference." A narration from Amr bin Abdullaah states that after Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) distributed wealth for the first time, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said to him, "Why do you not show preference to the earliest Muhaajireen and the earliest Muslims?" Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) responded by saying, "Should I buy from them the lead they have?" He then continued to exercise equality whenever he distributed.[^4]
